text:
We checked “The Harbour club_amsterdam-zuid_ENG Folder” and found 2 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 2 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Font missing from the package
Frontify needs the font files to render the text, otherwise the template falls back to another font.
Where: fonts “BlairMdITC TT”, “Montserrat (OTF)”, “Stay Dreaming” and 1 more
• Make sure the font is installed or activated on your computer.
• Package again with File > Package with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".
Learn more

2. Text aligned to the baseline grid
Frontify doesn’t use InDesign’s baseline grid, so line spacing will change.
Where: paragraph styles “kop wit”, “kop goud”, “intro Harbour Club” and 1 more, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Indents and Spacing and set Align to Grid to None.
Learn more

May change how it looks

3. Hyphenation is on
Browsers hyphenate differently from InDesign, so lines may break in different places.
Where: paragraph styles “kop goud”, “Arrangement”, “prijs” and 4 more, used on pages 1–2
• In the paragraph style, go to Hyphenation and uncheck Hyphenate.
Learn more

4. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: paragraph styles “kop wit”, “kop goud”, “intro Harbour Club” and 6 more, used on pages 1–2
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
